<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Make hidden directories indexable per root. Discovery already has `DiscoverySettings.include_hidden` (default false, honoured at discovery.rs:829) but it is only ever built from the GLOBAL daemon config (`state.config.scan`, roots.rs:178 and watch.rs:275), so nothing an operator runs can index a repo whose code lives under a dot-directory. The pij repo keeps 563 of its 667 TypeScript files under `.pi/extensions/` — invisible to search on prod today (backlog row 125 / row 147 receipt). This packet adds `flowspace3 add --include-hidden`, persists the flag per root, threads it into every scan and watch of that root, surfaces it in status/tree, and proves it by indexing the pij extensions on the test daemon and finding an extension function by search.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- `flowspace3 add <root> --include-hidden` (and the daemon `/roots` body) records the opt-in per root; re-running `add` with the flag on an existing root flips it and enqueues the newly discovered files
- every discovery for that root (initial scan, re-add, the watcher's rescans) uses `include_hidden = global OR per-root`; `.git` stays refused regardless
- `flowspace3 status --json` and `tree` show `include_hidden` per root so an agent can see why a hidden path is or is not indexed
- the skip ledger names hidden-directory skips as a reason (`hidden`) so `add` output explains what a default add left out
- real usage: on the test daemon, `add ~/pi-hacking/pij --include-hidden` indexes the `.pi/extensions/pij/**/*.ts` files and a search for a named extension function returns its element

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- changing the global default (hidden stays off by default)
- indexing `.git`, `node_modules` or anything the deny list refuses
- a per-directory allow-list; the flag is per root only
- prod re-ingest — o-prime does that after merge and takes the receipt
